title: PR performance drift detector using stratified token-slicing and synthetic bursts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Context:
We need a CI-side detector that automatically rejects PRs introducing statistically significant performance regressions in tokens/sec or p95 latency for serving runtime changes. Existing gates focus on single-run baselines and coarse p95 checks. This ticket proposes a stratified token-slicing + synthetic burst harness and a sequential detection algorithm to reduce false positives while catching real regressions earlier in PR flow.

Goals:
- Detect meaningful regressions in throughput (tokens/sec) and p95 latency across representative slices (model, sequence length bucket, batch size) during PR runs.
- Keep run cost under target budget by using small, high-signal synthetic bursts + cached KV prefixes.
- Provide clear diagnostics in CI for developers: per-slice deltas, effect size, confidence indicator, and suggested triage steps.

Design overview:
1) Stratified workload slices: generate 6 canonical slices derived from production trace sampling: short (<=128), mid (129-512), long (513-2048) sequence buckets × single-batch vs batched (batch=8). Each slice has an associated sample set of 20 traces for the PR run.
2) Synthetic burst harness: for each slice execute 3 micro-bursts (duration 30s) with warmed KV cache where applicable. Micro-bursts are run in isolated ephemeral containers to avoid noisy co-tenants.
3) Metrics captured per request: tokens emitted, server-side p95 latency, end-to-end p95, CPU/GPU util, kernel selection path. Aggregate per-burst and per-slice distributions.
4) Baseline and sequential detection: maintain a rolling EWMA baseline per-slice weighted by recent successful CI runs and the last N nightly runs. Use a sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) combined with a Bayesian credible interval on tokens/sec ratio to decide if the PR sample differs from baseline. This keeps decision latency low while controlling type-I error.
5) Gating logic: a PR fails the perf gate if BOTH: (a) at least one high-impact slice shows tokens/sec drop >=5% with SPRT p-value <=0.01, AND (b) corresponding p95 latency increases by >=10% or absolute p95 crosses configured threshold for the model family. Otherwise the result posts warnings and links to full traces.
6) Fallback and rerun: if the detector flags a failure with borderline evidence, the CI job automatically launches a higher-fidelity rerun (longer bursts, 3x samples) and re-evaluates. If rerun is inconclusive, the result is non-blocking but tagged for manual review.

Implementation details:
- New benchmark runner binary (perf-ci-runner) built in Rust to reuse low-level perf counters and ensure reproducible scheduling.
- Runner collects structured JSON traces compatible with our observability pipeline (console-trace-v2).
- A lightweight payload generator seeds the cache using short prefix sequences exported from production traces (sanitized).
- Baseline store: extend the existing baseline service to expose per-slice EWMA state and historical distributions via a simple REST endpoint.
- Integrations: GitHub Checks API annotation on PRs, link to perf dashboard (internal), and GitHub action to gate merges.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI job executes for a sample PR in under 18 minutes with default micro-burst config and total cloud cost under $3 per run.
- Detector identifies a known synthetic regression injected in a canary branch (test vector) with p<=0.01 and fails the PR consistently.
- Diagnostic output contains per-slice tokens/sec delta, p95 delta, effect size, and link to raw traces.
- Rerun path functions and upgrades an initial borderline failure to either fail or pass with clear reason.
- Baseline store exposes per-slice EWMA and last-10-run distributions in the console.

Risk & tradeoffs:
- Small sample sizes reduce cost but increase variance; hybrid approach (SPRT + Bayesian credible intervals + rerun) mitigates this.
- Synthetic bursts may not expose some production contention patterns; we will complement with periodic nightlies that run full replay profiles.
- False positives from environment noise: use isolated containers and stable kernel selection in the CI runner to reduce noise.

Next steps / implementation plan:
- Week 1: prototype perf-ci-runner and slice definitions; basic metric collection (ENG).
- Week 2: implement SPRT + EWMA baseline service endpoints (ENG + infra).
- Week 3: GitHub checks integration, posting, and initial PR gate experiment with a small set of repo owners (eng-sig).
- Week 4: iterate thresholds based on canary injection tests and initial developer feedback; roll to broader teams.

Notes about observability and triage:
- Provide an auto-generated triage checklist when failures occur: reproduce locally with perf-ci-runner, attach trace, run longer sample rerun, check kernel-change log.
- Store kernel selection info with each trace to quickly spot regressions tied to kernel/path changes.
